Narr rule for L1 fact rows (SS 2026-10-01): fact_value_text is the datum; citation_human is the sentence; verbalising an L1 fact value states a computed value, so a writer that composes citation_human from a fact value is declared (per writer, with the composed sites cited); the shared fact_value_text / formula_provenance_text columns stay undeclared (their strings are mixed values and labels). A citation that is only an identity (an entity name, a period lord-chain/level/ayanamsha, a fixed ordinal) is not narration. Version 1.7.0 (SS N-72 S2, N-73): the per-asset `carriage` object may also declare the asset's ONE carriage check ({applies: D1|D2|D3, nature: transcription|computation|derivation|ratified_judgment, why, evidence, spec (D1), citation_state (transcription), ruling (ratified_judgment)}); the validator refuses a nature/check mismatch (transcription -> D1, computation -> D3, derivation -> D3). As of 1.10.0 only bg_phaladeepika_latta declares one: an asset without it reads exactly as before. Version 1.8.0 (SS N-72 S3, N-73 (1)/(4), N-74 (b)): two more optional per-asset objects, each reviewed and carrying `why` (ONE line) and `evidence` (an existing repo-relative file[:line], or `unverified:<where>`). `vocab_alias` is {na: no_alias_class} (the asset has no vocabulary that could carry synonyms; refused at measure time where the table carries the documented alias column `synonyms`, N-73 (4)) or {class: planet, vocab_column, alias_column?} (the vocabulary column is measured against bg_ontology: canonical id and display name, and the ontology synonyms when an alias column is declared; without an alias_column the check reads at most PARTIAL, identity only, unless the declaration states `identity_only: true` with an `identity_only_why`; refused beside an alias-like column such as `synonyms`). `ldgr_source` is {na: no_classical_claim} (the asset states no classical rule or cited fact; refused where the asset declares a transcription carriage or the table carries a recognised citation column) or {source_column, citation_state: sourced|sourced_ocr_unverified|unsourced|refuted} (the column that carries the source and the state it stands on; an unsourced or refuted state can never read PASS, and a placeholder such as `not traced` is not a source, N-73 (1)). `why` must be a real one-line reason (at least 15 characters and 3 words, no placeholder word, no control or line-separator character); `evidence` a line within the real line count of an existing repo file, or `unverified:<a real description>` (never for an N/A release). The declared Ldgr check reads the whole table (every chart of a chart-scoped asset; for a shared table, rows other assets wrote), and only a text, varchar, text[] or json(b) column can carry a source. N/A is reached only through these declared words, never from a column pattern. As of 1.10.0 only bg_phaladeepika_latta declares either: an asset without them reads exactly as before. 1.9.0 (E6 S1, SS N-72 S1, N-73, N-74; REGISTRY_REVISION 13): one more optional per-asset object, `null_convention`, reviewed and carrying `why` (ONE line) and `evidence` (an existing repo-relative file[:line], or `unverified:<where>`): {table (an owned table), nullable: [{column, means (what NULL means, not a placeholder), scope?: {key_column, null_for: [key values], mode: only|exactly}}], constants: [{column, why, value?}], allowed_literals?: [{column, values, why}] (a value that looks like a placeholder but is a real value of a NON-nullable column)}. `no literal fallbacks` uses S3's placeholder definition on every text-like column of the table (text, varchar, citext, enum labels, domains over text; arrays element-wise, with allowed_literals compared per element), and on JSON columns at EVERY depth: a JSON null, an empty object or array, or any nested JSON null or string leaf that is a placeholder ({"src":"N/A"}, ["none"], {"a":null}, [null]) is a fallback; numeric and boolean arrays are not (an empty array is, and a 0 element only in a declared-nullable numeric array); an array whose element contents are not inspected (jsonb[], composite[], inet[], bytea[], uuid[], date[]) is tested for emptiness only and is listed as NOT examined (never counted in the 'no literal fallback' claim); boolean, date and timestamp columns cannot hold a literal fallback and are listed as not examined for it. The verdict also names every allowed_literals exemption in force and the columns whose constants were not examined (json, bytea / tsvector / vector, numeric arrays: cost). The Null cap lifts for the asset only when schema_default and blank_rows are clean and the detector verifies, read-only, that NULLs occur only in declared columns (and only on / exactly on the declared keys), that no declared-nullable column holds a literal fallback in place of NULL, and that no column is constant unless declared constant; a defect flips the Null cell to FAIL, anything else keeps the cap. As of 1.11.0 only bg_phaladeepika_latta declares one: an asset without it reads exactly as before. Version 1.10.0 (DECL-LATTA): bg_phaladeepika_latta's entry ONLY gains three reviewed declarations on the shapes S2/S3 verified: `carriage` (D1, transcription, citation_state sourced_ocr_unverified: both chunk ids, the Sloka 42-44 span, the per-claimant {clause, effect} pairs side by side; the passage is read from classical_text_chunks by span; only the declared clause/condition strings are quoted), `vocab_alias` (planet class on graha, identity_only) and `ldgr_source` (verse_ref, sourced_ocr_unverified; verse_ref names the counting-rule sloka range, it is not effect-precise); no null_convention and no other asset or structure changed. REGISTRY_REVISION 15 (STAMP; the file version is NOT bumped by this change, sequenced separately): `null_convention` may also carry `stamp_columns: [{column, why}]` (optional, at most 16; `why` a real one-line reason), a declared word for a WRITE-TIME stamp column (e.g. created_at, one seed transaction, one value on every row). The detector requires each stamp column to be a timestamp or timestamptz (the catalog type, domains resolved) AND NOT NULL (catalog constraint) with no NULL row and no infinity, -infinity or value at or before epoch + 1 day (epoch, 1970-01-01, year 0001 and earlier; counted in the column's own type), and exempts it from the constant test ONLY; nothing else is exempted (every other column is graded exactly as before, the literal-fallback test included). A stamp column that is nullable or not a timestamp is refused (the census reads NO_DETECTOR with the disagreement, never PASS); one holding a NULL row, infinity, -infinity or a value at or before epoch + 1 day fails the convention. A column may be declared once across nullable, constants and stamp_columns, and may not be a scope key_column, an allowed_literals column or a declared prose field. Version 1.12.0 (NARR-GUARD, N-94): bg_phaladeepika_latta's entry ONLY declares prose_fields [] (evidence_kind writer; its text columns are hand-typed restatements of passage clauses, not generated prose) together with `prose_coupling: {to, columns, why, evidence}`, a new optional per-asset object (field list `prose_coupling_declaration_fields`). `to` is `carriage_d1`, the only detector a prose N/A may rest on; `columns` lists the text columns classified as transcription; `why` must cite carriage transcription and Carr.D1; `evidence` must be an existing repo file:line (`unverified:` is refused). The validator refuses a coupling unless prose_fields is declared as an empty list ([]), the asset declares a transcription carriage that applies D1 with a spec, and every listed column is covered by that spec (derived from the spec, not from the declaration: the effect column and the passage_text extra fields; a claim field, an `equals` constant or a column the spec never checks is not coverage). The census then reads the four Narr checks N/A for such an asset only while its own Carr.D1 reads PASS; Carr.D1 PARTIAL, FAIL, NO_DETECTOR or ERRORED (a citation_state unsourced or refuted included) reads Narr NO_DETECTOR, never N/A. The coupling is inert for an asset that does not declare it (the four earlier prose_fields [] assets are unchanged); no other asset or structure changed. The coupling is bound by validation: an entry that declares prose_fields [] beside a transcription carriage checked by D1 is refused unless it also carries prose_coupling (the four earlier [] assets declare no carriage check and are untouched). Classification completeness is the declarer's: the columns listed in prose_coupling are the ones the guard verifies against the D1 spec and Carr.D1's per-row results; a text column the declaration leaves unlisted is only reported on the measured record (unclassified_text_columns), never gated, and the pin test on the committed entry is what guards the list. DENS-TIER-GUARD (1.13.0, SS ruling N-98): an entry may carry `density_tier_columns`, a list of {column, why, evidence} (field list `density_tier_declaration_fields`) naming the verification or confidence tier columns the asset's served select carries. The Dens tier vocabulary is a CLOSED list: a column counts as a tier only when it is named `tier` or `verification_pass_status`, or the asset declares it here, and never when its name carries a deny-listed word (cost, price, pricing, plan, access, subscription, billing, fee, tariff, in any spelling): a declared `cost_tier` is refused. The validator refuses a malformed list, a duplicate, more than 16, a weak `why` (it must say the column is a verification or confidence tier), an `evidence` that is not a real repo-relative file:LINE (never `unverified:`), a `why` naming a deny-listed word, an evidence file that does not mention the column, and, at measure time, a column that is not in the asset's table or a declaration that cannot be checked (no target table, or the catalog lists no columns): Dens.served reads NO_DETECTOR. A deny-listed word is matched in any spelling (underscores, digits, camelCase, plurals, run together with tier). The key is inert until an asset declares it. Version 1.14.0 (C1-1 Carr harness, N-101): the D1 `spec` may also carry `non_claim_columns: [{column, why, evidence}]` (at most 16; `why` a real one-line reason; `evidence` an existing repo file:line, never `unverified:`; the `why` or the evidence line must name the column as a whole token): the text columns the asset declares it makes no claim about (a key, a provenance pointer). The census column ledger (column types read from pg_catalog) requires every text-like column of the table to be matched by the D1 kernel, a declared constant (an `equals` extra), a declared non-claim or a declared prose field, else Carr.D1 cannot read PASS and names the column; a column of a type the ledger cannot class caps the verdict too, and a row_scope pin does not classify a column.
